style: Say smoothly and warmly, like an audiobook narrator
lines: The garden club has an empty bed, and Friday the council decides what grows there. Your quest: bring them a plan. Tap a question card to begin.
Stop one. Tap the question you will research.
Stop two. You have time for four visits. Tap four places.
Four places. Press Go.
Stop three. Tap one of the five ways to write this note.
Now press Save note, or Save note with its source.
Tap a place in your pack to write another note.
Four notes saved. Press On to Stop 4.
Stop four. Tap a note, then tap a heading. Then tap up to three plan steps.
Tap a heading to place this note.
Your outline is ready. Press Done.
Friday. The council is waiting. Press Next question to hear them.
Press Next question to hear the next council member.
Press See the decision to hear the council outcome.
Each line leads back to the choice that decided an answer. Tap a line to see that choice.
Plan approved! Next week the club plants native milkweed and fall flowers.
Approved, with homework: come back with the missing pieces.
Not yet. The council asks you to dig deeper and come back next month.
Some of your notes sound almost word for word. Try saying it your own way.
Your question is in the pack. Press On to Plan, or tap another question card.
That's a topic. A topic is a place to start. What do you want to know about it?
That's a question you can answer, and it's about our garden.
People can disagree on that one. Can research settle it?
You could find that out. Will it help the garden?
Principal Okoro. What are you asking us to do, and why?
Lily Tran. Why milkweed? Why not just pretty flowers?
Mr. Hale. Will the plants you want grow here?
Principal Okoro. Where did that fact come from?
Lily Tran. When should our flowers bloom?
Mr. Hale. Hold on. Is that really what your source said?
Mr. Hale. What plants are in Butterfly Blend?
